assumptions.text: The language is Rust. The ticket of this step states it, README.md names it, and every existing crate is Rust. The framework is none: plain Rust with rusqlite for the ledger, as horch-core uses today.

Each context is 1 module under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain/, application/ and adapters/ submodules (decision D1, understand N6). Existing modules (taskledger, vcs, runtime, roster, harness, routing, workspace) are wrapped by adapters and are not moved in this plan.

Attempt and its Lease are entities and value objects inside the Task aggregate, not their own aggregate (decision D2), because 04 S7 needs the end of the attempt and the requeue of the task in 1 ledger transaction.

Only the verification module can construct a VerifiedVerdict value, and Task::mark_done takes one; the one-door transition table also refuses verifying -> done with any cause other than verifier (decision D4, define N1).

Concurrency inside the ledger needs no optimistic retry: from Phase 5 fleetd is the single writer and runs its pass serially, and part 2 of a pass is 1 transaction (connect D1, design A24, A36). In Phases 1 to 4 the horch commands also write, through the same transition(). Each aggregate still carries a version, and the one-door transition checks from_state and the fleetd generation, so a stale write fails loudly.
The attempts table holds task attempts (written by task-execution) and sub-orchestrator attempts with task_id null (written by ideas). Each context writes only its own row kind (organise N2).

The platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform with its root at crates/horch-platform/src/: lib.rs holds the 1 interface and the NotSupported value, and mac.rs, linux.rs and windows.rs implement it (design A19, understand N13). It depends on no crate of the workspace, no context owns it, and each context calls it directly (decompose N7, strategize N1). Only these files hold OS cfg in production code (PL-2).

The implementation plan follows the 9 phases of the design migration plan in order: Phase 0, Phase P, then Phases 1 to 7 (design A19, A22, understand N19). Slice numbers follow the phases, and the Phase P slice comes right after the Phase 0 slice, so a slice is released only when its gate passes (design D9).
The fitness tests extend crates/horch-core/tests/arch_scan.rs, which already scans source files for forbidden lines. No new tool is needed.
Coined terms Verified Verdict, Stall Rung, Judged Tree, Path Claim, Awake Instant and Judge Finding name value objects and an entity that the canvases describe but do not name.

worker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper and the command start-agent-process (decision D3 option B, connect N5). The wrapper builds the private config home, scrubs the environment, maps CLI events, writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, and calls the platform interface for the process group and kill. Its composition root stays crates/horch/src/cmd/fleet_run.rs.

ideas takes the pattern domain-model, the most demanding pattern of its subdomain (strategize D1 option C). Only the plan validation module has an aggregate, Plan. Idea intake and questions stay active-record records in IdeasStore.

integration asks worktree-custody for each rescue ref through an in-process call (port RescueRefGateway), because worktree-custody alone writes refs under refs/horch/rescue/ (define N5, N6). No new cross-process message exists for it.
The 1 needs-you list belongs to ideas (decompose N9). task-execution publishes task-escalated and writes no needs-you file; ideas puts the task on the list beside approvals and escalated questions.

The Phase 0 list of expected failures is a file in the repository that the test runner reads. Each entry names a test and the phase that makes it green. The design does not name the path, so the plan names none.

Long work is a job (design A23, A32, A33). fleet-runtime owns the job runner (jobs table, run number, abandoned run limit, horch job requeue) and offers it to the other contexts as the driving port JobQueue. Each context queues its own job kinds in part 2 of a pass and reads their results in part 1 of a later pass (decompose N11, connect N11). No context port that runs git on a working tree, git on the network, a check or a gate runs inside a pass.

The bundle is an aggregate of integration with its own state machine (building, gating, passed, landed, failed, dropped), because strategize N5 names the bundle and feature state machines as aggregates of integration and the design gives the bundle its own table (A27, A34). It takes build-bundle, run-fast-gate and bisect-bundle with their events from the task-branch candidate of discover. A bundle and its member task branches change in the 1 transaction of part 2 of a pass (A24).

The sub-orchestrator answers a worker question with horch idea note, a file of class worker in its idea folder, read through IdeaFolderIngest. Only requests of class operator use the command channel, and each carries request_id and the operator token (design A35; connect N9).

coined_terms.definition: The value that only the verification module can create, and the only input that moves a task to done.
1 step of the stall ladder: first doorbell, second doorbell, or end of the attempt.

A time reading of awake machine time from the platform layer, used only by the hang check of fleetd and max_minutes of the fleet-run wrapper (PL-4, A25). Each other timer is a deadline on the fleet clock.
The set of paths a running task owns; 2 running tasks of 1 feature never hold overlapping claims.
1 miss that a judge task reports, with a rank of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.
The tree hash that a check, a review or a gate judged; a pass stands only while the tree is the same.
The map from each requirement of an idea to the tasks of its plan that cover it; a plan with an uncovered requirement is refused.
The link from a judgment-kind task to its judge task in another session, on another provider when the roster has one.

deprecated.reason: Attempt is an entity inside the Task aggregate (decision D2): 04 S7 needs the attempt end and the task requeue in 1 transaction.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): worker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper. Recorded in D3 (option B) and A11.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): an arch_scan rule enforces the context boundaries. Recorded as the test fitness_no_context_touches_foreign_tables in fleet-runtime.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): the agent status of herdr is the connect message agent-status-changed into task-execution and ideas. Both consume it idempotently.

Answered (orchestrator, D15): task branches rebase at landing, and a rebase of a feature branch does not wait for running attempts. Recorded in the integration test feature_rebase_during_running_attempt_then_landing_rebases_or_conflicts.
Answered (operator, D16): all 178 production sites move behind the platform layer in Phase P, between Phase 0 and Phase 1. Recorded in A7, A8 and the Phase P slice.
Idea intake stays active-record (strategize D1 option C, orchestrator D15; strategize N2): its commands are transaction scripts over IdeasStore.
Questions stay active-record (strategize D1 option C, orchestrator D15; strategize N2): its commands are transaction scripts over IdeasStore.

Answered by the design (A31, A33; organise N3; decompose N11): docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules as a docs_sync job, then a conformance job. worker-profiles owns both job kinds, marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, and a drift becomes an idea through ideas.
fleet-runtime is active-record (strategize N2): the jobs table is a record with invariant tests, and observe-jobs and requeue-job are application services over FleetRuntimeStore.

aggregates.name: Plan
invariants: I3: every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled
A plan is committed all-or-nothing after every validator check passes (FR-3, FR-4)
A judgment-kind task without a paired judge refuses the plan
The task dependencies of a plan form a graph with no cycle (FR-3)
A plan of a project with no declared fast gate is refused
A task is replanned at most once
A plan change that would leave a judgment task with no judge task is refused (A34)
state_transitions: none -> submitted (submit-plan, plan-submitted)
submitted -> committed (validate-plan, every check passes; plan-committed writes all tasks in 1 transaction)
submitted -> refused (validate-plan, any check fails; plan-refused carries the reasons)
refused -> submitted (submit-plan, a revised plan with a new content hash)
committed -> committed (replan-task, once per task; the changed plan passes the same checks; task-replanned)
rejected: committed with an uncovered requirement, a cycle, a judgment task without a paired judge or no declared fast gate
rejected: a second replan of 1 task
rejected: a replan that leaves a judgment task with no judge task (A34)

domain_services.name: PlanValidator
domain_services.description: Schema, DAG, coverage, profiles, model guide, paired judges, declared gates and citations to approved assumptions; pure over plan.yaml and the requirements. The Plan aggregate calls it before it commits.

application_services.name: AddIdea
application_services.description: horch idea add "..." or -f notes.md, optional --to <feature>. A policy also issues it for an adapter drift that conformance finds. An idea of a feature waits in captured while another idea of its feature is in clarifying, specifying or ticketing (A28).

application_services.name: StartSubOrchestrator
application_services.description: fleetd starts 1 fresh process per phase in the pane of the feature, and restarts a dead or missing one on the next pass. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after commit (connect N3).

application_services.name: AskOperator
application_services.description: 1 question at a time: what done looks like, scope edges, constraints, affected areas, priority.

application_services.name: AnswerInterviewQuestion
application_services.description: The operator answers in the pane. horch idea note records it.

application_services.name: AmendIdea
application_services.description: horch idea amend <id> "...".

application_services.name: WriteAssumptions
application_services.description: Writes assumptions.md: [confirmed] and [assumed] items, none [open].

application_services.name: RequestApproval
application_services.description: Moves the idea to awaiting_approval and notifies the operator. Reminds once an hour in working hours.

application_services.name: ParkIdea
application_services.description: Issued by policy after 7 days of waiting or an escalation. The operator also runs horch idea park.

application_services.name: CancelIdea
application_services.description: horch idea cancel, an operator request with request_id and the operator token. A policy also issues it when the feature of the idea is abandoned. Publishes idea-cancelled, and task-execution cancels each task of the idea that is not terminal (A34).

application_services.name: ReviseAssumptions
application_services.description: horch idea revise <id> "...".

application_services.name: ApproveAssumptions
application_services.description: horch idea approve <id>. Refused inside any fleet attempt; profiles deny it. fleetd writes approval.json with the sha256 the operator saw; any other approval file is ignored (I7).

application_services.name: AddDirectIdea
application_services.description: horch idea add --direct <ticket file>, optional --to. Refused inside a fleet attempt.

application_services.name: WriteSpec
application_services.description: Writes spec.md and requirements.yaml after approval.

application_services.name: SubmitPlan
application_services.description: Writes tickets and plan.yaml.

application_services.name: ValidatePlan
application_services.description: The plan validator: paired judges, declared gates, model guide, overlapping paths. Commits tasks in 1 transaction.

application_services.name: AskQuestion
application_services.description: Writes 1 question file, commits work in progress, exits.

application_services.name: AnswerQuestion
application_services.description: fleetd starts the owner on each pass until an answer is recorded. 4 cases (design, Ideas, How a worker's question is resolved). The sub-orchestrator answers with horch idea note, a file of class worker in its idea folder; it never uses the command channel (A35).

application_services.name: EscalateQuestion
application_services.description: Fires when the time limit of the question row passes.

application_services.name: ReplanTask
application_services.description: Once per task.

application_services.name: RollUpIdea
application_services.description: in_progress to integrating.

application_services.name: CloseIdea
application_services.description: Needs every worktree of the idea removed.

ports.name: IdeasCommands
ports.description: one operation per use case; called by the command channel (operator requests of horch idea ..., each with request_id and the operator token), the reconcile pass and the idea folder ingester

ports.name: IdeasQueries
ports.description: read models IdeaBoard, InterviewRecord, InFlightDiffs, ApprovedAssumptionsAndSpec

ports.name: IdeasEventHandlers
ports.description: policies on feature-opened, replan-requested, task-branch-landed, feature-merged, task-escalated (onto the needs-you list) and agent-status-changed (sub-orchestrator pane state); also feature-abandoned (cancel its ideas), task-branch-repair-escalated, job-abandoned and adapter-conformance-failed (onto the needs-you list, or a new idea for a drift)

ports.name: IdeaFolderIngest
ports.description: assumptions.md, spec.md, requirements.yaml, plan.yaml, question files and the answer notes of horch idea note; 1 ingestion per (path, sha256); a file of class worker is read only as a regular file, not through a link, under its size limit (SR-6)

ports.name: IdeasStore
ports.description: active-record rows of idea intake and questions: ideas, requirements, questions and sub-orchestrator attempt rows (task_id null)

ports.name: EventPublisher
ports.description: writes the event row in the same ledger transaction

ports.name: LaunchEnvironmentGateway
ports.description: asks worker-profiles for the idea-lead launch environment

ports.name: AgentProcessGateway
ports.description: sends start-agent-process to worker-profiles to start or stop the sub-orchestrator pane; never inside a ledger transaction

ports.name: NeedsYouInbox
ports.description: the 1 needs-you list (OR-3): approval requests, parked ideas, escalated questions, escalated tasks, escalated task branches, abandoned jobs, illegal transitions; each item has a stable key (its kind and its row) and a state open, resolved or superseded, and a producer writes by key (A28); herdr notification

ports.name: AttemptContext
ports.description: tells whether the caller runs inside a fleet attempt, so approve and --direct refuse there

ports.name: Clock
ports.description: deadlines on the fleet clock: the 30 min idle stop and the question time limit; calendar time: the 7 day park and the hourly reminder (PL-4, A25)

ports.name: PlanRepository
ports.description: load and save Plan with its PlannedTasks by idea id and content hash

ports.name: IdeaFolderWriter
ports.description: writes plan.verdict.json (plan-verdict-written) and approval.json (assumptions-approved) into the idea folder, atomic; fleetd is their only writer

aggregates.name: Task
invariants: I1: each live attempt of a task has exactly 1 unexpired lease; each leased or running task has exactly 1 attempt with a live process or pane; a resolver or fix attempt of a task branch holds the lease of its task while it is live

I2: no task is ready while a dependency is not met; an after: dependency is met when its task is done and its task branch is landed, a judges: dependency when the judged task is in verifying and its structural check passed
Only a VerifiedVerdict from the verification module moves a task to done (RR-3, define N1)
A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal (04 S7)
The outcomes asked, quota and critical_open burn no attempt (RR-11, A26)
An operator requeue resets the attempt count through attempt_floor (04 L8)
A task has at most max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then escalation (RR-6)
Each task state that is not terminal has an exit to cancelled; fleetd first stops the process group of a live attempt, and the cancel of a judged task also cancels its judge task (A34)
A resolver or fix attempt of a done task never moves the task; its failure or its lease expiry adds 1 to repair_attempts of the branch (A34)
Each operational timer of a task is a deadline on the fleet clock: the lease, each stall rung, the start timeout, the retry backoff and not_before (PL-4, A25)
state_transitions: pending -> ready (promote-task, each dependency met: done and its task branch landed; a judge task when its judged task passed its structural check)
ready -> leased (dispatch-task, the fleet clock is past not_before and no hold on dispatch applies; lease and worktree row in 1 transaction)
leased -> running (the first heartbeat of the wrapper; assign-task, start-work and launch-attempt run only after the worktree_add job passed)
leased -> ready|failed (no first heartbeat within the start timeout, outcome timed_out, or the worktree_add job failed, outcome crashed; rung 6)
running -> running (renew-lease, earned activity only)
running -> stalled (the lease expires on the fleet clock, or apply-stall-ladder)
running -> verifying (a valid result.json; write-result alone never leaves verifying)
running -> blocked_on_user (a valid question file, outcome asked, no attempt burned)
running -> ready (move-to-fallback onto a fallback persona of another provider, outcome quota, no attempt burned)
running -> waiting_quota (move-to-fallback with no fallback on another provider, outcome quota, lease paused)
stalled -> ready|failed (end-attempt stops the process group, rung 6; schedule-retry sets not_before while attempts remain)
stalled -> verifying (a valid result.json present in the same pass)
verifying -> done (mark-task-done with a VerifiedVerdict only; a judged task only after its judge task is done)
verifying -> ready (the judge reports an open CRITICAL item: a fix attempt, outcome critical_open, no attempt burned)
verifying -> ready|failed (the check or the review scripts fail, outcome rejected, rung 6)
blocked_on_user -> ready (question-answered or own-assumption-recorded)
waiting_quota -> ready (promote-task on quota-window-reset: reset_at passes, or with no reset_at the pool probe reports ok)
failed -> ready (the sub-orchestrator replans the task 1 time; attempt count 0)
failed -> escalated (escalate-task after its 1 replan, past replan_limit, or rescue-failed)
escalated -> ready (requeue-task by the operator, attempt_floor reset)
done -> done (requeue-task by the operator: repair_attempts of its task branch to 0 and 1 more resolver or fix attempt)
any non-terminal -> cancelled (cancel-task: a replan that replaces the task, horch task cancel, or the cancel or abandon of its idea or feature; the process group of a live attempt is stopped first)
rejected: done from any state without a VerifiedVerdict
rejected: ready while a dependency is not met
rejected: leased for a worker that already runs an attempt (I4)
rejected: an attempt counted for outcome asked, quota or critical_open
rejected: a done task moved by the failure of a resolver or fix attempt

aggregates.name: Verification
invariants: A verdict is verified only when result.json validates and the check passes in the worker sandbox
A code kind is verified only after the review scripts pass (V-14 limits)
A judgment kind is verified only with no open CRITICAL judge finding
The judged task stays in verifying until its judge task is done; a fix round is a new attempt of each, counted in fix_rounds of the judged task, at most 2, then both tasks go to escalated (A26, A34)
A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW finding
The check runs as a task_check job outside the pass, through the launcher, with the check timeout as its time limit (A23)
state_transitions: pending -> checking (run-check queues a task_check job; result.json validates)
checking -> check_failed (the task_check job ran to its end and failed, check-failed)
checking -> pending (the task_check job ended abandoned; it has no verdict and runs again)
checking -> reviewing (check-passed, code kind)
checking -> awaiting_judge (check-passed, judgment kind: structural check; the judge task is promoted)
checking -> verified (check-passed, judge kind: structural check only)
reviewing -> verified (review-passed)
reviewing -> review_failed (review-failed)
awaiting_judge -> verified (the judge task is done with no open CRITICAL item)
awaiting_judge -> critical_fix (open-critical-fix, fix round 1 or 2; a new attempt of the judged task and of its judge task)
critical_fix -> awaiting_judge (fix written, a fresh judge checks the earlier CRITICAL items only)
critical_fix -> escalated (a CRITICAL item left after 2 fix rounds; the judged task and its judge task go to escalated)
rejected: verified from pending, checking without a passed check, or awaiting_judge with an open CRITICAL item

domain_services.name: DispatchPlanner
domain_services.description: Picks ready tasks for workers across Task instances: I4, path overlap (04 L6), exclusive tasks, health guards and pool pacing. Pure: takes snapshots and a Clock reading.

domain_services.name: StallLadder
domain_services.description: Maps a liveness snapshot (process alive, heartbeat age, activity age, agent state) and an awake-time reading to the next rung: doorbell, doorbell, end.

application_services.name: PromoteTask
application_services.description: pending to ready when every dependency is done, or waiting_quota to ready when the pool resets.

application_services.name: DispatchTask
application_services.description: No cap. Only the holds on dispatch apply: the health guards (free disk, load), the pacing of the pool, an unhealthy profile and not_before. horch status shows each hold with its cause (A28).

application_services.name: LaunchAttempt
application_services.description: Starts the wrapper and the CLI in its own process group. A resume after an answer also launches. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after the ledger transaction commits (connect N3, N4). The attempt waits for the worktree_add job of its worktree; the lease and the start timeout start only at the launch (A32). A resolver or fix attempt of a done task launches the same way (A34).

application_services.name: RenewLease
application_services.description: Every reconcile pass (5 s). The lease is a deadline on the fleet clock, so a sleep never expires it (PL-4, A25).

application_services.name: ApplyStallLadder
application_services.description: Every pass: doorbell, doorbell after 2 min, then end. stall_after default 5 min; start timeout 90 s.

application_services.name: MoveToFallback
application_services.description: Fallback persona on another provider, else waiting_quota with the lease paused.

application_services.name: WriteResult
application_services.description: horch result writes outbox/result.json. Records the result on the Attempt. It never moves the task to done (define N1).

application_services.name: RunCheck
application_services.description: The verifier queues a task_check job, keyed by the tip of the task branch and the hash of the check, with today's check timeout (20 min, max 24 h) as its time limit. A passed or a run-to-the-end failed result is used again (A23, A33).

application_services.name: RunReview
application_services.description: Today's review scripts, unchanged. Rounds: light 1, full 3.

application_services.name: WriteJudgeVerdict
application_services.description: The worker of a judge task writes its verdict file.

application_services.name: OpenCriticalFix
application_services.description: At most 2 fix rounds.

application_services.name: SettleHighFinding
application_services.description: Fix or dismiss with a written reason.

application_services.name: EndAttempt
application_services.description: Stops the process group through the platform layer (Linux: SIGINT, 20 s, SIGKILL).

application_services.name: ScheduleRetry
application_services.description: Reads max_attempts and backoff from the profile.

application_services.name: EscalateTask
application_services.description: Publishes task-escalated with its reason. ideas puts the task on the 1 needs-you list (A14).

application_services.name: RequeueTask
application_services.description: Operator request with request_id and the operator token. An escalated task: resets attempt_floor. A done task: repair_attempts of its task branch goes to 0 and 1 more resolver or fix attempt starts; the task stays done (A34).

application_services.name: MarkTaskDone
application_services.description: The verifier writes verdict.json. Takes a VerifiedVerdict; only the verification module can construct one (D4).

application_services.name: AssignTask
application_services.description: fleetd writes task.yaml for the attempt from the committed plan, after the worktree_add job passed and before the launch. It is atomic and never rewritten; a change is a new attempt (connect A10).

application_services.name: StartWork

A gate pass goes stale when either judged tip moves (04 F5)
A feature is stacked on at most 1 older feature
A feature has 1 of 4 states, open, ready, merged and abandoned; merged and abandoned are terminal, and only the operator sets abandoned (A28, A34)
fleetd does not queue a rebase of a feature branch while 1 of its bundles is in gating or in passed (A34)
A merge with ideas in flight moves those ideas to a new feature (A28, A34)
With remote = none, fleetd does not fetch, push or open a pull request; the pull request state follows the feature state (A28)
A failed push sets push_state failed and push_not_before; at 3 failures in a row, 1 item goes on the needs-you list (A33)
state_transitions: open -> open (rebase-feature-branch queues a rebase job, rescue ref first, not while a bundle is gating or passed; a conflict opens a resolver task)
open -> open (stack-feature after trial-merge-conflicted)
open -> ready (mark-feature-ready: each idea of the feature integrating, cancelled or parked, and a current full gate pass)
open -> merged (check-merged finds the feature tip in the primary branch by content; move-ideas-to-new-feature for each idea in flight)
ready -> open (reopen-feature: its tip or the fetched primary tip moves, or a new idea is accepted with --to; the pull request becomes a draft)
ready -> merged (check-merged finds the changes by content)
open|ready -> abandoned (abandon-feature by the operator; a rescue ref for each branch that is not landed first)
rejected: ready without a current full gate pass
rejected: merged read from the GitHub API alone
rejected: rebase with no rescue ref of the old tip, or while a bundle of the feature is gating or passed
rejected: abandoned set by fleetd

aggregates.name: TaskBranch
invariants: I8: a task branch is landed only when its changes are in the feature branch by content
I11: every fleet branch in git has a branches row; one without is adopted as an orphan row, never deleted
I12: a branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it; a task branch is a member of at most 1 bundle that is not ended
A task branch is ready only when its task is done (verified)
Under the land lock, just before the fast-forward, the task is still landing and held by its worker (04 F9)
A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7)
An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator and only after worktree-rescued (connect N4)
conflicted and gate_failed are owned by fleetd; a failed resolver or fix attempt adds 1 to repair_attempts, and at max_attempts the branch goes on the needs-you list (A27, A34)
A branch of a cancelled task is abandoned only after its rescue ref is written (A34, connect F10)
state_transitions: building -> verifying (the task moves to verifying)
verifying -> ready (mark-branch-ready on task-done; a judged task only after its judge task)
verifying -> building (the check fails and a new attempt starts)
ready -> in_bundle (build-bundle, queue order)
in_bundle -> landed (its bundle passed and the move of the feature ref by compare-and-set is observed)
in_bundle -> ready (its bundle is dropped, or the bisect finds it clean)
in_bundle -> gate_failed (bisect-bundle finds it failing; a fix attempt of its task with the gate output, task-branch-gate-failed)
in_bundle -> conflicted (a conflict when the candidate is built; a resolver attempt in its worktree)
conflicted -> ready (the result of the resolver attempt passes its check)
gate_failed -> verifying (the result of the fix attempt passes the check)
conflicted|gate_failed -> conflicted|gate_failed (a failed resolver or fix attempt: repair_attempts + 1, the next one after the backoff)
conflicted|gate_failed -> needs-you (escalate-task-branch at max_attempts, task-branch-repair-escalated; horch task requeue starts 1 more)
building|verifying -> abandoned (the task is cancelled: rescue-worktree, then abandon-task-branch after worktree-rescued)
conflicted|gate_failed -> abandoned (horch branch abandon by the operator, after worktree-rescued)
any not landed -> abandoned (horch feature abandon, a rescue ref first)
rejected: ready while the task is not done
rejected: landed for a cancelled task (04 F9)
rejected: deletion without landed, merged or rescued
rejected: a member of 2 bundles that are not ended

aggregates.name: Bundle
invariants: fleetd writes the bundles row and its bundle_members rows in 1 transaction before the bundle_build job (A27)
A bundle moves the feature ref only by compare-and-set from its base tip; a failed compare-and-set drops the bundle and its members go back to ready (I9, A34)
A task branch is a member of at most 1 bundle that is not ended (I12)

fleetd deletes the candidate ref refs/horch/bundle/<id> of a landed, failed or dropped bundle when no child bundle of it is building, gating or passed, and reads the ref store again to verify the deletion (A34)
The fast gate runs once on a bundle, as a fast_gate job keyed by the candidate tip and the base tip (A23, A33)
state_transitions: none -> building (build-bundle: bundles and bundle_members rows, then 1 bundle_build job)
building -> gating (the bundle_build job passed; run-fast-gate queues the fast_gate job)
building -> dropped (a member conflicts, the job failed for another cause, or the feature tip moved; members back to ready, a conflicting member to conflicted)
gating -> passed (the fast_gate job passed)
gating -> failed (the fast_gate job failed; bisect-bundle into child bundles, the failing branch to gate_failed)
gating -> dropped (the feature tip moved; members back to ready)
passed -> landed (the move of the feature ref by compare-and-set is observed; each member to landed)
passed -> dropped (the compare-and-set fails because the feature tip is not the base tip; members back to ready)
rejected: a feature ref move that is not a compare-and-set from the base tip
rejected: a candidate ref deleted while a child bundle is building, gating or passed

application_services.description: horch branch abandon, an operator request with request_id and the operator token, or a policy on task-cancelled and feature-abandoned. Sends rescue-worktree and moves the branch to abandoned only after worktree-rescued.

application_services.name: RunTrialMerges
application_services.description: Each in-flight feature against the primary branch and against each other in-flight feature. Queues 1 trial_merge job per pair, keyed by the 2 tips; git merge-tree with no checkout; records TrialMerge with its job (A23).

application_services.description: Asks worktree-custody for a rescue ref of the old tip first (RescueRefGateway, A13), then queues a rebase job. Not while a bundle of the feature is gating or passed (A34). Does not wait for running attempts; their task branches rebase at landing.

application_services.description: Queues the full_gate job of the feature, keyed by the feature tip and the fetched primary tip; once when its tasks are landed, again when a pass goes stale.

application_services.description: features.state open to ready.

application_services.description: pr setting gh or manual. Not with remote = none. The pull request state follows the feature state (A28).

application_services.name: MergePullRequest
application_services.description: On GitHub, or a plain git merge. The default merger is the operator. Runs only when the project pr setting lets fleetd merge; by default the operator merges and check-merged observes it.

application_services.name: CheckMerged
application_services.description: Every pass reads git, not the GitHub API.

application_services.name: EscalateTaskBranch
application_services.description: Puts a task branch on the needs-you list when repair_attempts reaches max_attempts of the profile. Publishes task-branch-repair-escalated (A34).

application_services.name: FetchRemote
application_services.description: Queues 1 fetch job for each repository at each fetch period (fetch_period_s), also after a failed run. The job records each remote tip in remote_tips. Not with remote = none (A23, A33).

application_services.name: PushFeatureBranch
application_services.description: Queues a push job of the feature branch with --force-with-lease on seen_remote_tip. Each retry is a new run after push_not_before; at 3 failures in a row, 1 needs-you item (A33).

application_services.name: ReopenFeature
application_services.description: Moves a ready feature back to open when its tip or the fetched primary tip moves, or a new idea is accepted with --to; its pull request becomes a draft (A28).

application_services.name: AbandonFeature
application_services.description: horch feature abandon, an operator request with request_id and the operator token. Writes a rescue ref for each branch that is not landed, moves each such branch to abandoned, and publishes feature-abandoned (A28).

application_services.name: MoveIdeasToNewFeature
application_services.description: When a feature is merged with ideas in flight, opens a new feature and moves each such idea to it (A28, A34).

decisions.question: Where do the 6 context modules live in the existing crates?

options.summary: New modules crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain, application and adapters; existing modules become adapters behind the new ports.
pros: Matches understand N6: contexts are modules inside horch-core
Clear seam for the fitness tests
Existing tests of taskledger and vcs keep running while phases land
cons: 2 code paths exist until each phase retires the old one
Adapters wrap code that is not hexagonal
risks: Old and new paths drift if a phase leaves the old one in place

options.summary: Evolve existing modules in place: taskledger becomes task-execution, vcs becomes integration, and so on.
pros: No wrapper code
1 code path at all times
cons: Existing modules mix concerns of several contexts (taskledger holds worktrees, landing and tasks)
No place for the dependency rule
risks: A large refactor before Phase 1 can start

options.summary: A new crate horch-fleetd that horch depends on.
pros: Compiler-enforced boundary to horch-core
cons: Cyclic needs: fleetd adapters wrap horch-core modules and horch-core tests need fleetd
risks: Build time and a crate split nobody asked for

decisions.rationale: understand N6 puts the contexts inside horch-core, and the migration plan replaces old behaviour phase by phase, so the old modules must keep working behind adapters until their phase retires them.
would_flip_if: The operator wants a crate boundary enforced by the compiler
A phase retires a whole existing module at once, so wrapping it costs more than moving it

decisions.question: Is Attempt its own aggregate or an entity inside Task?

options.summary: 3 aggregates as discover proposes: Task, Attempt, Verification.
pros: Small aggregates
Attempt rows of sub-orchestrators fit without a task
cons: 04 S7 needs the attempt end and the task requeue in 1 transaction, which crosses 2 aggregates
risks: A crash between the 2 writes loses the requeue (the #216 bug)

options.summary: Task holds its Attempts and the Lease; Verification stays its own aggregate.
pros: 04 S7 and I1 are 1-aggregate transactions
A task has at most max_attempts attempts, so the aggregate stays small
Verification runs long checks outside the task transaction
cons: Sub-orchestrator attempts (task_id null) are not part of this aggregate and are written by ideas
risks: Task grows if attempts keep transcripts; they must keep only ids and outcomes

options.summary: 1 Task aggregate that also holds the verification state.
pros: 1 aggregate for every task fact
cons: A 20 min check holds the task aggregate
The only-the-verifier-sets-done rule has no module seam
risks: define N1 is harder to prove

decisions.rationale: 04 S7 is a preservation row: the reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal. With 1 aggregate per transaction, the attempt must be inside Task. Verification stays apart so the verifier is the only module that can produce a VerifiedVerdict (define N1).
would_flip_if: The ledger allows a multi-aggregate transaction as an explicit exception for the reap
Attempts must carry large state such as transcripts

decisions.question: Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper logic (connect D2)?

options.summary: task-execution: the wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, which are task-execution facts.
pros: The files it writes feed the lease and the stall ladder
cons: task-execution would start processes, against connect N3
risks: The process-group and sandbox code leaks into a core context

options.summary: worker-profiles: the wrapper builds the private config home and maps CLI events per adapter.
pros: Per-CLI event mapping sits with the harness adapters
cons: worker-profiles would own a process role and the 256k context guard at run time

options.summary: fleet-runtime: the wrapper is a process role of the binary, like fleetd and fleetd check; it asks worker-profiles for the CLI event map.
pros: Process groups, the platform layer and atomic file writes already live there
Keeps both core contexts free of process code
cons: fleet-runtime is already the largest supporting context
risks: The CLI event map crosses from worker-profiles at run time

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Chosen: B. Reason of the orchestrator: the wrapper is the profile made real (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping), and the scrub needs 1 owner. Process group and kill go through the platform interface, which each context calls. This differs from the recommendation of this step. The step recommended C: Recommended option C. Strongest argument against it: fleet-runtime then owns 4 process roles and the team has high cognitive load (organise warning).

notes_for_downstream.text: The code step adds no message across a process boundary. start-agent-process and launch-environment stay in-process calls into worker-profiles (port AgentProcesses and LaunchEnvironmentQuery). The file protocol (task.yaml, START.md, result.json, exit.json, heartbeat.json, verdict.json, plan.verdict.json, approval.json, idea-folder files), the command channel, herdr agent status and GitHub are the contracts that need schemas.

Each contract test name in code.json is 'contract: <message id>' and each idempotency test is 'idempotent: <message id>'. ddd-contracts should use the connect payloads of these messages and the idempotency keys as written.

Contract and idempotency tests now quote the connect payloads in the snake_case names of the design. New tests: contract for assign-task, start-work, task-verdict-written, heartbeat-written, plan-verdict-written, assumptions-approved and open-pull-request; idempotent for pull-request-merged, agent-status-changed, heartbeat-written and task-escalated.

worker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper (D3 option B), so heartbeat.json and exit.json have worker-profiles as producer and task-execution as consumer, and the contract entries heartbeat-written and attempt-exited carry the domain of their producer. The command channel tests are request_with_a_seen_request_id_returns_the_stored_result, known_request_id_with_another_payload_hash_is_refused and refused_request_returns_its_reason in fleet-runtime.

The platform layer (crates/horch-platform) and the in-process rescue ref call from integration to worktree-custody are code seams, not wire contracts. Cover them with the fitness and module tests named in code.json.

Each operator request (the 6 of round 2 and cancel-idea, cancel-task, requeue-task, abandon-feature, requeue-job, drop-rescue-ref) carries request_id and operator_token in place of idempotency_key, and its response has state applied or refused, result when applied and reason when refused (A24, A35).

New contract tests in code.json: idea-cancelled, task-cancelled, worktree-rescued, task-branch-gate-failed, task-branch-repair-escalated, feature-abandoned, push-feature-branch, attempt-exited, adapter-conformance-failed, profile-marked-unhealthy, profile-marked-healthy, job-abandoned and job-requeued. Only the operator requests, pull-request-closed, push-feature-branch, observe-jobs and run-conformance-tests cross a process boundary.
answer-question is a file of class worker that horch idea note writes in the idea folder; it never uses the command channel and carries no operator token (A35, A18).

plain_words.what: This step turns the 6 parts of the fleetd design into a code plan for Rust: which folders, which types, which interfaces, which tests, and in which order to build them. It writes no code.
plain_words.decided: All 6 parts live as modules under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/. The OS-specific code lives in its own small crate, crates/horch-platform, that every part calls. 3 parts get aggregates (rich objects that guard their own rules): Task and Verification in task-execution, Feature and TaskBranch in integration, and Plan in ideas. An attempt lives inside its task, so a crash can never end the attempt and forget the task. worker-profiles starts every agent process and owns the per-attempt wrapper. The build order is the 9 phases of the design, with Phase P (moving the OS code) right after Phase 0. Every slow piece of work (a check, a gate, a trial merge, a rebase, a git fetch or push, a worktree add or remove) runs as a job outside the 5 s pass, so a long gate never makes fleetd look hung. Integration gets a third aggregate, Bundle.
plain_words.assumed: We assumed the existing modules stay where they are and get wrapped, not moved. We also assumed nothing else may mark a task done: only the verifier can create the value that does it. Integration asks worktree-custody for each rescue ref instead of writing it itself.
plain_words.riskiest: Wrapping old modules means 2 code paths live side by side until each phase removes the old one. If a phase forgets to remove its old path, the old watchdog and the new fleetd can both act on 1 task. Phase P moves 178 OS-specific sites at once; its only safety net is that every test gives the same result before and after the move. The job runner is new and every context depends on it: if a job result is used again when it must not be, a failed push or fetch never runs again.
